title: docs(types): cite the retire-vs-remove discriminator once instead of restating it at eight sites (objectui#9684)
body:
Part of #9684 — this PR takes the live half and hands the rest back as a decision; the card stays open for it.

> ## RE-DERIVED AT HEAD `baa386c4b` — one vintage, no stale sentence left standing
>
> Written by the implementer in the same push that created this head. ⭐ Round 5 established the rule this body follows: the whole body is ONE vintage, every figure re-derived against the head being pushed, and a sentence the review falsified is **repaired in place** rather than annotated. ⛔ Nothing is left for a banner to excuse.
>
> **What round 5's review falsified, and what became of it here:**
>
> 1. "caught only directly behind `or`, with nothing but a comma, whitespace and an opening parenthesis allowed in between" — that named a **set** while the pattern `,?\s*\(?` required an **order**. ⛔ **Repaired by moving the pattern, not the sentence** — see A below. The sentence now reads "any number of them, in any order", and it is true.
> 2. "Its population is every comment in the package" — two ABUTTING comments were one block, so a drifted copy inherited its neighbour's precondition. ⛔ **Repaired in the code** — see B below.
> 3. "Ablation ledger — 17 legs" beside a paragraph enumerating 18. ⛔ **Repaired by re-deriving the number from the table**, which is now 41 and is counted from the rows below rather than remembered.
>
> ⚠️ Round 5's body also carried this sentence: "⛔ The clause pattern itself is **unchanged**; nothing was widened to make a sentence true." **That is no longer true, and round 6 reverses that choice on purpose.** The reversal and its four-axis reasoning are stated below rather than quietly dropped.

Clause-②: yes

## What round 6 changed

Round 5's contract review passed the direction for the fifth time and reproduced every figure the round printed — the pin, the reverse leg, the full suite, the 65-file `.d.ts` equality with both marker controls, the population at base and head, and the exact failure sets for B1, C1, C2 and D1. Standing A, standing B/③C and ③D are all **closed**. Two findings remained, both in the **silent** direction, both wordings nobody had tried.

**A · the separator sentence named a SET; the pattern enforced an ORDER.** All four carriers said `3`, `iii`, `third` and `thirdly` are caught behind `or` "with nothing but a comma, whitespace and an opening parenthesis allowed in between" — a set of permitted characters. The pattern spelled that separator `,?\s*\(?`, which admits **comma, then whitespace, then parenthesis, in that order only**. So `, or ( 3 ) …` (whitespace *after* the parenthesis) and `, or ,3 …` (a comma *after* whitespace) contained nothing any published sentence forbade and passed **22/22**.

⛔ **The sentence was not patched to describe the order.** The separator is now `[\s,(]*` — the genuine set its prose always claimed — and the caught-list in all four carriers is **re-derived from the widened pattern**, 20 wordings re-measured through the pin (legs W01–W20), never hand-patched. Two properties make that safe and checkable:

- `[\s,(]*` is a strict **superset** of `,?\s*\(?` — every string the old separator admits is made only of commas, whitespace and opening parentheses ⇒ ⛔ **no wording that was caught became silent.** Measured, not argued: the eight previously-caught wordings are all still caught (W09–W15, W20), and the four wordings the header declares silent are all still silent (W05–W08).
- The two escapes now red (W01, W02), and so do the two further set-shaped spellings nobody had published either: `, or, (iii) …` (W03) and `, or (( 3 )) …` (W04).

⚠️ Two observations the review asked to be folded in, both measured here: `, and prong-3 keeps …` is **silent** (W19) — the hyphenated spelling is not `prong 3` and ⛔ no carrier claims it is; and `, or third-party tooling keeps …` **reds** (W20) — the anchor catches a non-numbering `third` behind `or`. That second one is the **declared spurious-red direction** and is fine by design: a spurious red sends a human to read four blocks, a spurious green is the defect this pin exists for.

**B · two abutting comments were ONE block, so a drifted copy inherited its neighbour's precondition.** A blank line was the only thing that ended a comment run. So an un-amended `//` statement wedged between the `ChatbotSchema` JSDoc's closing delimiter and `export interface` — no blank line — passed **22/22**, and so did an un-amended JSDoc stacked directly above that JSDoc. A human reads five statements; the pin counted four.

⭐ The pin's own prose already forbade exactly this: *"A blank line ends a run on purpose — joining across one would let a drifted note inherit a compliant neighbour's precondition and pass."* The code joined across `*/`→`//` and `*/`→`/**` anyway. ⛔ The prose was right; the **code** now says it — the same direction ③D took. A run now ends at a `*/` and starts at a change of kind.

⚠️ That is a **boundary** rule, ⛔ not a rule about statements, so it re-cuts every abutting pair in the package. Re-derived at this head with the pin's own comment oracle rather than remembered:

| abutting shape, no blank line | sites in `packages/types/src` |
|---|---|
| `*/` → `//` | **3** (`spec-ui-namespace.ts:32`, `zod/objectql.zod.ts:679`, `zod/objectql.zod.ts:1904`) |
| `*/` → `/**` | **13** |
| `*/` → `/*` | **1** (`field-types.ts:903`) |
| `//` → `/**` | **11** (`complex.ts` ×2, `index.ts` ×5, `layout.ts`, `objectql.ts` ×2, `zod/objectql.zod.ts`) |
| `//` → `/*` | **1** (`index.ts:1326`) |
| **total** | **29** |

The block count over the package goes **4696 → 4725** — one new cut per pair, exactly — and ⛔ no count anything asserts moves: the same **4** statements at the same four line spans (`complex.ts` 165, 1026, 1381, 1830), **9** trailing comments, **0** of them stating the rule, before and after.

⚠️ **A figure in the round-5 handoff that this round could not reproduce, stated rather than quietly corrected.** The handoff recorded this census as "`*/`→`//` with no blank **0**, `*/`→`/**` with no blank **0**, `//`→`/**` with no blank **5** (`index.ts` 1085, 1129, 1170, 1224, 1428)". Measured here package-wide, those are **3**, **13** and **11**; the named 5 are the `index.ts` subset of the third row, and every site listed above was read back by eye with `cat -A` before being reported. ⇒ the fix was verified against the real 29, ⛔ not against the 5.

## What the card asked for, and what the tree says now

The card measures one live defect on PR #9682's head `dce4a74a1`: the sixth statement of the retire-vs-remove discriminator, the `GestureConfig` note in `mobile.ts`, did not carry the amended surviving-carrier precondition.

⚠️ **That instance is already repaired, and it was repaired before #9682 merged.** #9682 landed as `5f8190c8cc98409e65400ff24adfb805b80a3ffc` at 2026-09-17T11:56:43Z — thirty minutes after the card was filed — and its merged diff amends the `GestureConfig` note along with the other four. Read on this branch's base `fc12bc8c6`, that note states the amended rule in full.

⭐ **The card's class is live anyway, at two sites the card did not name.** Re-derived on `fc12bc8c6`, which is still this branch's merge-base with `origin/main` at this head:

| file @ `fc12bc8c6` | retirement it argues | carried the precondition? | in the card's six? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `complex.ts` block opening at :165 | `KanbanColumn.color` | yes | yes |
| `complex.ts` block opening at :1026 | `ChatbotSchema` dark keys | yes | yes |
| `complex.ts` block opening at :1381 | `displayMode` | yes | yes |
| `complex.ts` block opening at :1830 | `triggerIcon` | yes | yes |
| `mobile.ts` block opening at :74 | `MobileResponsiveConfig` | ⛔ **no** | ⛔ **no** |
| `mobile.ts` block opening at :122 | `MobileOverrides` | yes | yes |
| `mobile.ts` block opening at :293 | `GestureConfig` | yes (by `5f8190c8c`) | yes |
| `mobile.ts` block opening at :371 | `MobileComponentConfig` | ⛔ **no** | ⛔ **no**

Every address above is bound to `fc12bc8c6`; none of them is carried into any file in this diff. The same population read at this head is **four**, all in `complex.ts` — which the pin asserts rather than this table.

So the population was **eight**, not six, and the amendment reached five of eight. ⇒ the card's own argument holds harder than it claimed: the failure is not "one site was missed", it is "the instrument that enumerates the sites is itself a phrase grep, and it undercounts".

## The widened scan, and its controls

⛔ The card's six were not treated as a closed list. Scans, all bound to `fc12bc8c6`:

- **Concept scan, whole tree** (not just the two files, not just the package): `git grep -inE "steers? authors to|named live replacement|keeps? loud|kept loud|taught as working|surviving carrier|no carrier"` over every tracked file. Lit control: it fires well outside the two files — `packages/app-shell/.../FlowNodeConfigField.entryCondition.test.tsx`, `packages/types/src/__tests__/page-breadcrumbs-refusal-8871.test.ts`, three more test files, `scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs`, and **five** `.changeset/*.md` bodies (`4919`, `5942`, `7519`, `7678`, `9183`) — so its zero elsewhere is a reading, not a silent probe. ⚠️ Rounds 1–5 printed "four `.changeset/*.md` bodies" here; re-derived at `fc12bc8c6` in this push it is **five**, and the list is now named rather than counted from memory.
- **Route-argument scan**, for paraphrases that state the rule without any of those phrases: `git grep -inE "rather than (a )?tombston|rather than kept as|removed outright|outright rather than|than a plain removal|never. carcass|tombstone (exists|is available|rather)"` over `packages/types/src` excluding tests and `zod/`. This is the scan that found `MobileComponentConfig`, which paraphrases the precondition as *"There is no surviving object to hang a `never` key on"* and is invisible to every phrase the card's probe searched for. Lit controls in the same pass: it fires on `ai.ts` and on `objectql.ts`, neither of which the card names.
- **Two sites outside the card's two files, reported and deliberately NOT changed**: `AIFormAssistSchema.formId` in `ai.ts` cites *"PRONG 2 of the discriminator (objectui#5941, #7526, #7678)"* without restating it — it is already the shape this card asks for, and it needed no edit when #7678 amended the rule, which is the measured precedent for the remedy below. `ObjectKanbanSchema.allowCollapse` in `objectql.ts` argues "why a tombstone rather than a plain deletion" from the passthrough silent-keep mechanism; that is a different argument, not this discriminator, so it is a boundary case, not a ninth site.
- ⚠️ **A wrapping hazard the card's probe shares with any line-based grep**: `grep -inE` reads one line at a time, and this prose wraps mid-phrase. Live demonstration re-taken at this head on a sentence this PR must not disturb: `grep -c 'no silent-strip hazard for prong 2 to guard'` over `mobile.ts` prints **1**, while flattening the comment punctuation and line wrapping first prints **2** — the second occurrence wraps. The pin flattens before matching for exactly this reason.

## The change

`mobile.ts` now **cites** the rule instead of restating it. The statement it cites is the `ChatbotSchema` JSDoc in `complex.ts`; each of its four retirement notes points there and keeps its own per-retirement argument — which prong holds here and why — which no shared statement can carry, exactly as the card says. ⚠️ That is the statement they cite and ⛔ **not** the only one in the package: `complex.ts` states the rule at four sites, `ChatbotSchema` among three peers (`KanbanColumn.color`, `displayMode`, `triggerIcon`), and whether those four become citations too is the open decision below. Nothing is deleted into a vacuum: every prong measurement, reopen condition, spec-history note and ⚠️ carve-out is kept. The `MobileComponentConfig` note keeps its own precondition as the precondition rather than dropping it, with its wording brought to the amended form — "no surviving **object**" became "no surviving **carrier**", which is the rule's own phrasing and what the pin matches.

A file preamble states, once, where the rule lives and why this file cites while `complex.ts` states.

## Measurements — all re-taken on `baa386c4b`

**① The `.d.ts` asymmetry the card lists as "not measured".** `mobile.ts` argues its retirements in `//` comments; `complex.ts` argues its four in JSDoc on exported members. Declaration emit treats those differently. Measured by injecting one marker into each and rebuilding the package clean, under the verify lock:

| marker injected into | occurrences in the emitted declaration file |
|---|---|
| a `//` note in `mobile.ts` (present once in `src` in the same run) | **0** in `dist/mobile.d.ts`; per-file hash table unchanged vs the head table (**0** diff lines) |
| the `ChatbotSchema` JSDoc in `complex.ts` (present once in `src` in the same run) | **1** in `dist/complex.d.ts`, **0** in `dist/mobile.d.ts`; per-file table moves **4** diff lines |

⚠️ **A first attempt at these two legs measured nothing and is reported as such.** Both replacements re-emitted their own anchor, so `ablation-replace` refused the mutation ("the anchor count moved 1 -> 1, a drop of 0") and the build that followed carried **no marker at all** — a reading of `0` that would have read exactly like the real leg. ⛔ It is not counted as a measurement; the legs above are the re-run with consumed anchors, each with its `src` count printed beside its `dist` count so a zero cannot be an unplanted marker. Residual markers after the pass: **0** files in `src/`, **0** in `dist/`.

⇒ a citation costs a consumer of the published declarations **nothing** in `mobile.ts`, and would cost one a jump out of the block they are in for every site in `complex.ts`. That is the reason this PR converts one file and not the other.

**② What a `.d.ts` consumer's reading changes to: nothing.** Clean full rebuilds in one locked pass (`rm -rf dist` + `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types build`, then per-file `sha256sum` over `dist/**/*.d.ts`), never incremental: this head emits **65** declaration files, **130** files in `dist` total; with this branch's base `mobile.ts` (blob `5e3ad63df`) swapped in it emits **65**; the per-file hash tables differ by **0** lines and the set-hash is identical (`6774b4db26140485`). A third clean build after restoring the head file reproduces the first table exactly — **0** diff lines — so the equality is ⛔ not a stale-`dist` artefact. The instrument is the same one that scores 1 and moves the table by 4 lines for the `complex.ts` injection above, so it is ⛔ not a probe that cannot fire.

**③ Reverse verification of the pin, at this head.** Fix committed first, then `mobile.ts` alone written back to the base blob under a `trap ... EXIT INT TERM`, the pin re-run, then restored with `git checkout HEAD -- ABSOLUTE_PATH` (⛔ never a bare `git checkout --`, which restores from the index):

- **this head: 22 passed / 22.**
- **base `mobile.ts` swapped in: 8 failed / 14 passed.** The precondition assertion and the outside-`complex.ts` assertion both name exactly the four base blocks — `mobile.ts` blocks opening on lines **74**, **122**, **293** and **371** — found by an instrument that was not told where to look; the four citation assertions and both `mobile.ts` statement assertions fire alongside them. ⭐ Unchanged from round 5, which is the point: the boundary change re-cut 29 pairs and moved this reading by nothing.
- Landing proven by a changed blob (`1d33aebaece0` → `5e3ad63dfb29`) and by an on-disk count of a base-only phrase, ⛔ never by an exit code. Restore verified by blob hash (`1d33aebaece0` back to HEAD), an empty `git diff HEAD` and an empty `git status --porcelain`.

## The pin

`packages/types/src/__tests__/tombstone-discriminator-agreement-9684.test.ts` derives the population of rule statements from the source at run time. **Six `describe` blocks, 22 assertions at this head** — read off the file (16 `it` / `it.each` declarations, two of them `.each` over 4 cases). It fails when

1. any comment in this package states the rule without its surviving-carrier precondition **in the rule's own phrasing**,
2. any file in this package **outside `complex.ts`** states the rule at all — a prong, a clause, anything that matches its statement markers, in a comment of any form, including one riding on a code line and including one glued directly against a compliant neighbour,
3. any of `mobile.ts`'s four notes stops citing `ChatbotSchema`, or the citation target stops stating the rule,
4. `complex.ts` states the rule at any number of sites other than the recorded four, or at a site the roster does not name,
5. one of those four carries a clause its peers do not, and
6. the pin itself quotes the rule it guards.

Its population is every comment in the package. A comment run ends at a blank line, at a `*/` and at a change of comment kind, so two abutting comments are two blocks; a comment riding on a code line is its own one-line block. It carries its own controls: a synthetic un-amended statement that must be flagged, a synthetic amended one that must not, prose that merely mentions a tombstone that must stay out of the population, and two **vacuity controls** — the four published statements in `complex.ts` must still be found, and the roster must still resolve to four distinct blocks, so a marker that stops matching reds instead of quietly emptying every other assertion. ⛔ What it cannot do is named in its header rather than hidden: a NEW paraphrase past every marker is invisible to it, exactly as `MobileComponentConfig` was to the card's grep. "Is this span a comment" is answered by `scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs`, never by a private regex.

## Ablation ledger — 41 legs, every one restored and proven

⛔ No sentence above about what the pin catches is asserted; each is a hypothesis run through the pin. **41 = 6 pre-fix + 21 separator + 4 adjacency + 5 regression + 1 reverse + 4 `.d.ts`** — counted from the rows below, ⛔ not remembered. Every source mutation went through `ablation-replace` (literal anchor that must hit a declared number of times, on-disk landing proven by a **changed blob**, restore proven by blob equality plus an empty `git diff HEAD`). Working tree after every batch: `git status --porcelain` **0 lines**.

⭐ **Six mutations were REFUSED by the tool and measured nothing** — their replacements re-emitted their own anchor, so the anchor count did not drop and `ablation-replace` exited non-zero before any test ran. They are named here rather than silently re-run: the first attempts at E4, E5, B1, C1, C2 and the two `.d.ts` marker legs. ⛔ None is counted as a leg; each was re-run with an anchor the replacement consumes, and those re-runs are the rows below. That is the tool doing the job it exists for — a replacement that does not land produces a green that reads exactly like a pass.

### Pre-fix — the two escapes reproduced at `e39b1a8da`, the head round 5 reviewed

| leg | mutation | mutated blob | pin |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | `, or ( 3 ) …` on the `ChatbotSchema` statement | `3dd7dc9432a9` | 22/22 — **silent** |
| E2 | `, or ,3 …` on the same statement | `7858d7d5f1b5` | 22/22 — **silent** |
| E3 | un-amended `//` statement between the `ChatbotSchema` JSDoc's `*/` and the declaration | `2e66e693f106` | 22/22 — **silent** |
| E4 | un-amended JSDoc stacked directly above that JSDoc, no blank line | `deb6c5d5fbe7` | 22/22 — **silent** |
| E5 | **control**: the same stacked JSDoc **with** a blank line | `7568f7ec28b3` | **4 failed** |
| E6 | un-amended `//` statement above that JSDoc, no blank line | `46da257f395e` | **2 failed** |

E1 and E2 reproduce the review's blobs exactly. E5 is what says the instrument was not simply blind: separate the blocks by one blank line and it reds 4.

|---|---|---|---|---|

Every red names one assertion: *the `ChatbotSchema` statement carries exactly its recorded clauses*, listing `a-prong-beyond-the-two` present at one site and absent at its peers. ⭐ W05's blob `2a16978c2c0a`, W21's `04b3bc24932c`, W14's `607141edf530` and W15's `ad27035ae7dc` are the same blobs rounds 4 and 5 printed for the same mutations — an independent cross-check that these are the review's legs and not lookalikes.

### Adjacency — the same four mutations as E3–E6, re-run against the fixed pin

⭐ **The blobs are identical to the pre-fix rows**, so nothing about the mutation changed; only the pin did.

| leg | mutation | blob | pin before | pin after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | `*/` → un-amended `//` statement → declaration | `2e66e693f106` | 22/22 **silent** | **5 failed** |
| X2 | un-amended JSDoc stacked above, no blank line | `deb6c5d5fbe7` | 22/22 **silent** | **4 failed** |
| X3 | **control**: the same, **with** a blank line | `7568f7ec28b3` | **4 failed** | **4 failed** |

⭐ X2 and X3 now fail **identically** — that is the whole fix: a blank line no longer decides whether a drifted copy is seen. X4 was already caught and still is; it now reds through the substantive assertions (exact count, roster names, shared clauses, precondition) instead of only through the two `kind === 'jsdoc'` assertions, and the **11** real `//`→`/**` sites in the package are untouched by it — measured as the unchanged population above (4 statements, 9 trailing, 0 stating the rule) and by the pin's own 22/22 at this head.

| leg | plant | blob | pin |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | fully amended statement in `data-display.ts` | `f4e7332729c7` | **1 failed**, and exactly one: *no file outside `complex.ts` states the rule AT ALL* |
| B2 | same, precondition removed | `1b078ce7682d` | **2 failed**: that assertion plus the precondition assertion |

⇒ a dead marker cannot print the same quiet zero B1's assertion prints when the tree really is clean. All five readings are identical to round 5's.

### Reverse and `.d.ts` — 5 more

The reverse leg (③ above) and the four `.d.ts` legs: base-`mobile.ts` swap, third-build reproduction, the `ChatbotSchema` JSDoc marker control, the `mobile.ts` `//` marker control.

## Why this shape and not the others — the four axes

**Option A — amend the two stragglers in place** (the shape the card's remedy section refuses). **Option B — one block, every site cites it.** **Option C — cite where a declarations reader pays nothing, state where it pays, pin the agreement** (this PR). **Option D — pin only, leave all eight statements.**

**实际业务需求.** Measured, not assumed: the rule is stated in six of this repo's changeset bodies — `4919`, `5942`, `7519`, `7678`, `7703` and this card's own `9684`, the list that marker sweep prints rather than a remembered count, re-derived at this head — and it was amended once (#7678), an amendment that reached five of eight sites. So the recurrence is real. But the cost actually paid was a reader getting the WRONG rule, not an author paying for a slow edit ⇒ agreement is the demand, fewer copies is a means. And the consumer side is asymmetric by measurement ①: a `.d.ts` reader has never been able to read `mobile.ts`'s four. A remedy that charges that reader a jump to fix a problem they do not have fails this axis, which is what separates C from B.

**项目长远合理性.** N statements of one rule is the N-dialects shape AGENTS.md #0.1 refuses for metadata, and prose inherits the reasoning: one contract beats N. A is the patch that fails it outright — it grows N to eight-agreeing and makes the ninth amendment a nine-site edit. B is right in principle and wrong on the published face, because `complex.ts`'s statements ARE part of what the package publishes. C takes the principle exactly as far as the contract face allows and says so in the file. D leaves the structure that produced this card intact.
